controller_initialization_sequence: 1. PCIe enumeration: BIOS/OS enumerates the PCI Function, assigns BAR0/BAR1 (64-bit MMIO), enables Memory Space + Bus Master in PCI Command register, configures MSI-X capability.
2. Host driver reads CAP (offset 0h, 64 bits) — captures CAP.MQES, CAP.CQR, CAP.AMS, CAP.TO, CAP.DSTRD, CAP.NSSRS, CAP.CSS, CAP.BPS, CAP.MPSMIN, CAP.MPSMAX, CAP.PMRS, CAP.CMBS.
3. Host reads VS (offset 8h) — verifies major.minor.tertiary version is at least required version (e.g. 1.4).
4. Host disables controller: writes CC.EN = 0 (only if CSTS.RDY=1); polls CSTS.RDY → 0 within CAP.TO × 500 ms.
5. Host allocates Admin SQ + Admin CQ in host memory, each page-aligned per CC.MPS. Default size = 64 entries each (configurable up to 4096).
6. Host writes AQA: AQA.ASQS = SQsize-1 (0's-based); AQA.ACQS = CQsize-1.
7. Host writes ASQ = 64-bit physical base address of Admin SQ (lower 12 bits zero).
8. Host writes ACQ = 64-bit physical base address of Admin CQ (lower 12 bits zero).
9. Host writes CC: CC.MPS = log2(host_page_size) - 12; CC.AMS = arbitration; CC.CSS = NVM Command Set (000b); CC.IOSQES = 6; CC.IOCQES = 4; CC.SHN = 0; CC.EN = 1 (atomic 32-bit write).
10. Host polls CSTS.RDY until 1 (within CAP.TO × 500 ms); if CSTS.CFS=1 abort and re-attempt.
11. Host issues Admin Identify Controller (OPC=06h, CNS=01h): fills SQE in Admin SQ slot 0, writes SQ0TDBL=1.

12. Controller fetches SQE via PCIe MRd, executes, writes 4 KB Identify Controller structure to host PRP buffer via PCIe MWr, posts CQE to Admin CQ slot 0 with SQHD=1 and Phase Tag=1, asserts MSI-X vector 0.
13. Host reads CQE, verifies SC=0, writes CQ0HDBL=1 to release the slot.
14. Host parses Identify Controller: NN (max namespaces), SQES/CQES (required entry sizes), MDTS (max data transfer size), OAES (optional async events), CNTLID, etc.
15. Host issues Set Features Number of Queues (FID=07h, CDW11 = (NCQA<<16)|NSQA, 0's-based) to request desired I/O queue count; controller returns granted counts in CQE.DW0 (NCQA<<16)|NSQA.

16. For each desired (CQID, SQID) pair: issue Create I/O CQ (OPC=05h) first (PRP1 = CQ memory base, CDW10[15:0]=CQID, CDW10[31:16]=QSIZE-1, CDW11[31:16]=IV, CDW11[1]=IEN, CDW11[0]=PC); wait for CQE; then issue Create I/O SQ (OPC=01h) (PRP1=SQ memory base, CDW10[15:0]=SQID, CDW10[31:16]=QSIZE-1, CDW11[31:16]=CQID, CDW11[2:1]=QPRIO, CDW11[0]=PC).
17. Host issues Identify Active Namespace ID List (CNS=02h) to discover active NSIDs.
18. For each active NSID, host issues Identify Namespace (CNS=00h) to learn NSZE, NCAP, NUSE, LBAF[], FLBAS, MC, DPC, DPS, NMIC, RESCAP, NGUID, EUI64.
19. Controller is now in RUNNING state; host begins normal I/O against namespaces.
io_read_sequence: 1. Host allocates a data buffer of size NLB * LBA_size bytes, page-aligned.

2. Host fills an SQE in I/O SQy: CDW0 = OPC(02h) + FUSE(00b) + PSDT(00b) + CID; NSID = namespace; PRP1 = data buffer base; PRP2 = (page-aligned next page if 2-page transfer) or PRP List pointer if >2 pages; CDW10/11 = SLBA[31:0]/SLBA[63:32]; CDW12[15:0] = NLB-1; CDW12.PRINFO/FUA/LR per requirements; CDW13 = DSM hint.
4. Controller fetches SQE via PCIe MRd; decodes OPC=02h.
5. Controller reads data from NAND/SCM media into internal buffer.
6. Controller issues PCIe MWr TLPs streaming data to host PRP/SGL buffer (one or more TLPs per memory page; TLP size ≤ MPS).
7. Controller posts CQE to CQ ring: DW0 = command-specific (0 for Read), DW2 = SQID:SQHD (new SQHD), DW3 = SF:P:CID with SC=0 SCT=0 P=current Phase.
8. Controller asserts MSI-X vector configured for this CQ.
9. Host driver picks up the interrupt, reads the CQE, processes it, advances CQ Head, writes CQyHDBL = new Head.
io_write_sequence: 1. Host fills data buffer with payload to write.
2. Host fills an SQE in I/O SQy: CDW0 = OPC(01h) + FUSE(00b) + PSDT(00b) + CID; NSID = namespace; PRP1 = data buffer base; PRP2 = ...; CDW10/11 = SLBA; CDW12 = NLB-1 + FUA/PRINFO; CDW13 = DSM hint.
5. Controller issues PCIe MRd TLPs against host data buffer; receives Memory Read Completion TLPs with payload.
6. Controller writes data to NAND/SCM media; if FUA=0 may write into write cache; if FUA=1 commits before completion.
asynchronous_event_sequence: 1. After initialization, host issues one or more outstanding Asynchronous Event Request commands (OPC=0Ch) on the Admin SQ.
2. Controller holds the AER outstanding (no CQE posted) until an asynchronous event occurs.

3. On event: controller posts a CQE for one outstanding AER; DW0 = event class (Error Status 0h, SMART/Health 1h, Notice 2h, Reserved 3h..5h, Vendor Specific 7h) | log page identifier (e.g. 02h SMART) | event information.
4. Host reads CQE; identifies event class; issues Get Log Page for the indicated log; takes corrective action.
5. Host issues another AER to re-arm the channel.
controller_reset_sequence_cc_en: 2. Host writes CC.EN = 0 (preserving other CC fields).
3. Controller stops command processing; releases all I/O queues (Admin SQ/CQ remain); clears CSTS.RDY to 0.
5. Host can now reconfigure CC and re-enable.
shutdown_sequence_normal: 1. Host stops issuing new I/O commands.
2. Host completes outstanding I/O by polling CQEs and updating CQ Head.
4. Controller processes the notification: drains pipeline, flushes write cache to persistent media, updates persistent state (if any), sets CSTS.SHST = 01b (shutdown processing).
5. When complete, controller sets CSTS.SHST = 10b (shutdown complete).
6. Host may safely remove power or trigger PCIe Conventional Reset.
shutdown_sequence_abrupt: 2. Controller may begin flushing data using Power-Loss Protection (PLP) capacitors if equipped; may simply stop processing.
3. Controller sets CSTS.SHST = 10b without guarantee of drain.
4. Power may be removed; in-flight data may be lost.
nvm_subsystem_reset_sequence: 3. Subsystem performs NVM Subsystem Reset; all controllers in the subsystem reset (Conventional Reset to PCIe).
4. After PCIe link retraining and BIOS/OS re-enumeration, host reads CSTS — finds CSTS.NSSRO = 1 indicating last reset was NSSR.
5. Host re-runs the full controller initialization sequence.
firmware_update_sequence: 1. Host issues Firmware Image Download (OPC=11h) with portions of the firmware image; NUMD=CDW10 (Number of Dwords - 1); OFST=CDW11 (offset in Dwords).
2. Repeat for all chunks until full image transferred.

3. Host issues Firmware Commit (OPC=10h) with FS=target slot, CA=Commit Action (0h replace, 1h replace+activate-next-reset, 2h activate-existing-image-on-next-reset, 3h replace+activate-now without reset, etc.).
4. Controller commits firmware to selected slot; may require Conventional Reset, NVM Subsystem Reset, or live activation (per Firmware Activation Notice).
5. Host updates internal records based on CQE status.
create_io_queue_pair_sequence: 1. Host allocates CQ memory page-aligned, size = QSIZE × 16 B.
2. Host issues Create I/O CQ (OPC=05h, PRP1=CQ_base, CDW10[15:0]=CQID, CDW10[31:16]=QSIZE-1, CDW11[31:16]=IV, CDW11[1]=IEN, CDW11[0]=PC).
3. Wait for Admin CQE with SC=0.
4. Host allocates SQ memory page-aligned, size = QSIZE × 64 B.
5. Host issues Create I/O SQ (OPC=01h, PRP1=SQ_base, CDW10[15:0]=SQID, CDW10[31:16]=QSIZE-1, CDW11[31:16]=CQID, CDW11[2:1]=QPRIO, CDW11[0]=PC).
6. Wait for Admin CQE with SC=0.
7. Queue pair is now ready; host writes SQyTDBL / CQyHDBL to operate.
delete_io_queue_pair_sequence: 1. Host stops issuing new commands to SQy; waits for all outstanding to complete.
2. Host issues Delete I/O SQ (OPC=00h, CDW10[15:0]=SQID).
4. Repeat for any other SQs sharing the same CQ.
5. Host issues Delete I/O CQ (OPC=04h, CDW10[15:0]=CQID).
7. Queue pair resources are now released.
